Title: Punjab Highway's Delicious Butter Chicken: A Culinary Delight Punjab Highway, renowned for its authentic Punjabi cuisine, has truly outdone itself with its tantalizing Butter Chicken dish. As a connoisseur of Indian cuisine, I had high expectations, and I'm pleased to say that every bite exceeded them. From the moment the dish arrived at my table, I was struck by the inviting aroma of rich spices and creamy tomato sauce. The chicken pieces were succulent and tender, perfectly cooked and infused with the flavors of the marinade. The sauce itself was a masterpiece, striking the perfect balance between velvety smoothness and robust spices. What sets Punjab Highway's Butter Chicken apart is the depth of flavor. Each bite was a symphony of tastes, with hints of garlic, ginger, fenugreek, and a touch of sweetness, all complementing each other harmoniously. The texture was divine, with the creamy sauce coating every morsel of chicken, creating a decadent experience that left me craving more. Accompanied by freshly baked naan bread, the Butter Chicken at Punjab Highway is a complete meal that satisfies both the palate and the soul. The portion size was generous, ensuring that every diner leaves feeling thoroughly content. In addition to the impeccable taste, I was impressed by the restaurant's warm ambiance and attentive service. The staff were knowledgeable about the menu and eager to provide recommendations, enhancing the overall dining experience. In conclusion, Punjab Highway's Butter Chicken is a culinary masterpiece that deserves every bit of its acclaim. Whether you're a seasoned enthusiast of Indian cuisine or a newcomer eager to explore new flavors, this dish is sure to delight your taste buds and leave you craving another visit. I highly recommend Punjab Highway to anyone seeking an unforgettable dining experience filled with authentic flavors and warm hospitality.

Best food we have ever eaten. 40 countries and hundreds, if not thousands, of restaurants later - nowhere compares to Tamba. The staff are so friendly and caring, the food is on another level, the restaurant is beautiful - you literally just cannot fault it. Tamba is truly in a league of its own. If it weren't for COVID, it would probably be worth flying back to Abu Dhabi just for Tamba. Cannot wait to go again. If you ever get the chance to visit, go! You will not regret it, it is one of the best dining experiences you will ever have.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Panjab Grill restaurant and I must say that it was an outstanding experience from start to finish. This review aims to capture the essence of my visit and highlight the reasons why this Indian restaurant deserves accolades. From the moment I stepped inside, I was warmly greeted by the staff, who exuded genuine warmth and attentiveness. The ambience of the restaurant was elegantly decorated with subtle Indian-inspired touches, creating a soothing and inviting atmosphere. The menu offered an extensive range of both vegetarian and non-vegetarian delicacies, showcasing the incredible diversity of Indian cuisine. Exploring the flavors of India, I decided to sample a variety of dishes, including the curry, fragrant Biryani, crispy Vegetable Samosas, and a selection of aromatic Naan bread. Each dish was a delight to the senses. The flavors were robust, well-balanced, and authentically executed. The spices used were perfectly blended, infusing the dishes with a tantalizing complexity that had me wanting more with each bite. It was evident that great care had been taken in sourcing high-quality ingredients, resulting in dishes that were cooked to perfection. The attention to detail extended beyond the food itself. The presentation of each dish was visually appealing, adding to the overall dining experience. Additionally, the staff was prompt in clearing plates and ensuring a clean and tidy table throughout the meal.

If you're planning a romantic date night, Coya Restaurant offers a lovely atmosphere that's just perfect. The seafood options on the menu are delightful, with the calamari being a personal favorite, although I wished it had a bit more seasoning. The limited selection of nonalcoholic drinks was a downside for me. As the evening progressed, the music got louder, which I didn't quite enjoy. I found that coming around sunset was ideal, as you can enjoy the brilliant views of the restaurant without the noise becoming overwhelming. Despite these minor drawbacks, Coya is a charming choice for a special evening, especially for seafood enthusiasts looking for a romantic setting. Parking: Free valet parking service, just make sure you scan the valet card at the reception

We came here on WEEKDAY. Not too crowded but.. 7pm above is their peak hours. The food came little bit slow, the waiters aren’t so responsive. We need to rang the bell many times until they come. We offer you private and non private rooms. I got the private room for 6 persons. Jajangmyon was OK 7/10 (boiled egg OVERCOOKED) Chicken - TOO sweet, too much honey (i think so) so 7/10 Sosogi soup - spicy, odd but good. 8/10 but the tofu? Come on you can give us more. I only got 3 tiny cubes. Han-chi was good and refreshing 9/10 it is a fish soup and really good Godeong 10/10 ! Love it.. the taste, seasoning was legit. Nakji - is the squid leg 6/10 . Tooooo spicy for me, TOO much vegie and chili instead the octopus, they cut Really really small, so they trick you to think there is a lot of octopus on that big plate. And the PRICE, TOOOOOO WAYYY MUCH for the this menu. Price wise? Maybe because they are authentic cuisine they charge you little bit pricy. Parking lot was easy and plenty. You can seat outdoors too. They have a really big screen outside to enjoy. There is driving range if you like to play golf. Of course kids friendly ☺️ Kid-friendliness: Outside they have a really big field but NO playground Wheelchair accessibility: Not friendly

The dining experience was highly disappointing. I ordered beef sashimi, a Korean beef set, brisket soybean soup, steamed egg, and a bottle of Hwayo 53. Beef sashimi: I didn't even try it as the color of the beef was so dark. I've never had beef sashimi that looked like this, and I didn't want to risk getting sick. Beef sashimi or tartare should be made from the freshest beef available, but this was clearly not the case, as shown in the picture. Korean beef set: The meat quality was poor, with dark spots on the edges and chunks of fat that couldn't be grilled. To make matters worse, I found a piece of plastic in the meat. I even wondered if the meat was scraped from other tables. Despite trying to make the best of the dining experience, I had to stop eating when I saw other tables being served much better quality meat - pinkish red. The picture of the ungrilled meat clearly shows its subpar quality. Steamed egg: It was undercooked, with a thick top layer that was still raw. I had to dig to the bottom to find any edible part. I tried to mask the disappointment by drinking Hwayo, but the experience was too unpleasant to overcome. In a rare occurrence, I questioned the staff about why our dishes were so different from those at adjacent tables. They offered to waive the food charges, but I insisted and paid for everything to ensure I had the right to express my dissatisfaction.

The presentation of the dishes was particularly impressive, especially the fish.  We thoroughly enjoyed the opportunity to try Lebanese food, particularly the whole fish.  Above all, I really appreciated the staff's professionalism. I recently visited Beirut Sur Mer again and unfortunately had a disappointing experience with the service. While the ambiance and food quality were commendable, the service fell short of expectations. The waitstaff seemed overwhelmed, leading to extended waiting times for orders and difficulties in getting their attention for assistance. There were lapses in communication, which impacted the overall dining experience. The limited vegetarian options on the menu were disappointing. As someone who prefers vegetarian choices, I found the selection lacking and wished for more variety. I hope that the management addresses these issues as it has the potential to be a fantastic dining destination with improvements in the service department.

restaurant_name: Grimaldi's Pizzeria - Coal-Fired- Brick Oven Pizza
description: The new Pizza spot is in town! short review: food was great service was stellar atmosphere was cozy long review: their pizza is on the thinner side, quite uncommon around the city. but their toppings are of great quality, the pepperoni was salty (maybe too much if you’re looking out for your sodium.) but everything else was top-notch. their appetisers are to go for, usually i wouldn’t even order any cause its just expensive and is small. mushroom soup is made with wild mushrooms, mozzarella sticks were not as crunchy but served with a side of refreshing arugula salad. now the service was absolutely stellar. kimberly was attentive, polite, and absolutely pleasing. ask for her spot if you want amazing service like we got.

restaurant_name: Grimaldi's Pizzeria - Coal-Fired- Brick Oven Pizza
description: Milan and the rest of the staff were amazing! From the minute we stepped into the restaurant, we were met with 10/10 hospitality. The options on the menu were great. We tried the mozzarella sticks as a starter, a medium sized double pepperoni spicy honey pizza, and a medium sized pesto pizza with some grilled chicken and sun dried tomatoes as add ons. All 10/10. We were served complimentary cheesecake by Milan, such a considerate waiter. He kept checking in on us and making sure everything is okay. The atmosphere, as you can see in the picture, was cozy with a touch of retro. Downside is it’s in the middle of a mall, but you can always have their pizza for takeaway! Worth coming back for again, and again, and again, and again. Too good to gatekeep, try it out!

I can't recall ever having a bad meal at this restaurant.  I've visited multiple times for both lunch and dinner, trying the set menu both with and without added champagne. Sometimes I have walked in to check for available tables, and when none were free, I enjoyed a drink at the bar where smoking is permitted. The dishes are prepared with quality ingredients and are beautifully presented.  The flavors are layered expertly, offering a complex taste profile enhanced by aromatic seasonings and diverse ingredients.  The service here is excellent and has always been greatly appreciated.  If you want to be wowed and feel that you're truly getting your money's worth, I recommend giving them a visit.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Maharani Dawat in Abu Dhabi, and it was an exceptional experience from start to finish. The highlight of my visit was the Maharani Thali, which I wholeheartedly recommend to anyone looking to indulge in authentic and flavorful vegetarian Indian cuisine. Upon entering Maharani Dawat, I was immediately impressed by the warm and inviting atmosphere. The décor is elegant yet cozy, reflecting a perfect blend of traditional Indian aesthetics with modern comfort. The staff greeted us with genuine smiles and guided us to our table promptly, setting the tone for a delightful dining experience. The Maharani Thali is a culinary masterpiece, offering a generous assortment of vegetarian dishes that beautifully showcase the diversity and richness of Indian cuisine. Each item on the thali was meticulously prepared and bursting with flavor. From the aromatic vegetable biryani to the perfectly spiced curries, every bite was a testament to the chef's skill and passion for cooking. Particularly noteworthy were the paneer tikka masala and the dal makhani, both of which were cooked to perfection with a delightful balance of spices. The assortment of breads, including naan and roti, were freshly baked and complemented the dishes wonderfully. The thali also included a variety of chutneys and raita, which added a refreshing contrast to the rich flavors of the main dishes. The service at Maharani Dawat was impeccable. The staff was attentive without being intrusive, ensuring that our glasses were always filled and that we had everything we needed. They were knowledgeable about the menu and provided excellent recommendations.

I have ordered the Maharani Thali for a takeaway and the food was delicious, it was the best, it was better than some of the good hotels in India also, I am a North Indian, so I would request and recommend you if you are a North Indian don't go for it, because if you go once, you will get addicted to their food. Especially the Palau/Fried rice was amazing it was so delicious and its fragrance is unforgettable. If you are ordering a Maharani Thali, check the pictures and think again, can you eat them all, its a lot. But believe me once you start you can't stop. The food was magnificent. Unfortunately for me it was a takeaway and as you can see the box was huge and the restaurant didn't provide me with any carry bag, which was uncomfortable to take. So if you are trying a takeaway, try to take a bag or something to get it. And I would suggest the management, think about it, you provide great food probably the best in Abu Dhabi but you lack the basic carry bag facility, please rectify, Thank you But again I have to say the food was the BEST.

restaurant_name: Al Khayma Heritage Restaurant Abu Dhabi
description: One of the best restaurants we have ever eaten at. The portions were absolutely huge, we ordered the cold appetizers that came with bread, the stuffed lamb with rice, sparkling water and a green apple juice. I think that 5 people could have eaten it (we were 2 people). We also got chickpea soup and tea on the house. The service was amazing, Peter gave us excellent recommendations and was overall very pleasant and helpful. This is a must eat for everyone visiting the Grand Mosque as it's very close to it. I'd say this is a must eat period. A 10/10 restaurant.

restaurant_name: Al Khayma Heritage Restaurant Abu Dhabi
description: There were so many great reviews for this place that I was a bit sceptical that a food court restaurant could be that good, but it is. Staff were really helpful and knowledgeable in helping me choose a dish that was vegetarian and gluten free. I had a really tasty local rice dish with roasted vegetables, dried fruit and herbs and spices. The flavour was exquisite. It was actually the tastiest rice dish I have ever eaten. And the cost is not expensive. Many thanks for your hospitality and fine food.

restaurant_name: Al Khayma Heritage Restaurant Abu Dhabi
description: We visited here as part of a group trip and tour of the mosque, and I was’t expecting much as a result of it being the ‘encouraged option’. However what a mistake that was and if you’re wanting some traditional food in a casual and welcoming environment you should try it. There’s standard tables as well as traditional options with rugs on the floor, which is what make it one of the more authentic choices in the mall. The whole restaurant isn’t overly large but there’s a decent number of staff meaning you never have to wait long for service and they’re proactive too. The menu is full of clear photos to help deciding and the service time from the kitchen was quick considering how busy the place was. Portion sizes were huge and it felt like we’d ordered two sharing platters rather than two main dishes! Flavours were amazing with everything cooked perfectly. I was rather blown away seeing the huge number of positive reviews but they are indeed justified and I’d certainly return next time I’m in the mall.

Experience based on breakfast and diner The Pros: Ample Seating Space: Sofra Bld provides plenty of seating both indoors and outdoors, ensuring comfort and flexibility for diners. Extensive Buffet Selection: The buffet offers a diverse range of dishes, catering to various tastes and preferences, including both local specialties and international fare. Regular Replenishment: Throughout my visits, all sections of the buffet were regularly replenished, ensuring freshness throughout the dining experience. The Cons: Ingredient Quality: While the buffet offers a wide variety of dishes, I noticed that some ingredients could be of higher quality, potentially impacting the overall taste and dining experience. For example omelette at breakfast was not as good as in other hotels. Inconsistent Service: I've experienced inconsistent service, particularly in the evening, with no staff greeting diners upon entry, difficulty in obtaining the bill, and overall lack of attentiveness. Limited Lighting: The restaurant's limited lighting can create an ambiance that some may find too dark, potentially affecting the dining atmosphere. Presence of Birds on the terrace : Outdoor dining may be disrupted by the presence of many birds during the day Additional Charges for Drinks: Despite being an "all you can eat" restaurant, patrons are charged for all drinks, including water, which may come as an unexpected additional cost. Kid-friendliness: Plenty of food for the children, they will love the chocolate fountain Wheelchair accessibility: Restaurant can be accessed by lift from the lobby

Went in for my wife’s birthday date. I believe we came early as no one at the front desk, but we were greeted by a guest officer after a few minutes. The place is elegantly and luxuriously decorated. Numerous sittings with ample space in between the tables. So no need to worry to hit someone just incase the sitting got full. You may opt to be sat at their al fresco dining with the view of the marina and colorful (night time) Maqta bridge. The buffet was split into different sections. The bread and pizza section is sitting at the left side of the entrance. This area offers a variety of baked goods and hand tossed pizza with live cooking. You can basically see the chef tossing the dough, send it inside the oven and serve a steaming medium sized pizza. Pepperoni, vegetable and margherita was served that night. Next to it is the grilling section. They had a variety of tikka and kebab served, and you may choose  cuts of tuna, salmon and sea bass to be grilled. Doze it salt and pepper as you like. Right after the grilling section is the main dish area, where international cuisines were served. The selection was great, but the roasted beef ribeye is a lil bit chewy for a ribeye. The steamed veggies were nicely cooked. Not too crunchy and not too poachy. The salmon and chicken eere superb. At the end is the noodles, soup and seafood section. They served three types of soup, seafood tom yum was my wife’s must have. We’re not able to taste any of the noodles, since we had one a day ago. They have a few selections for seafood dishes, the sea-bass is not overdone. They also offer a live cooking for the seafood section, though they only had a few types of fishes offered that night. At the opposite side was the salad and sushi bar. You can watch the sushi chef prepared and hand rolled sushis. Right at the middle is the dessert bar. The area offers fresh cut and whole fruits, dates, a handful selections of arabic sweets, wide selection of ice cream, sorbet and frozen yogurt. You may also request a freshly made crepe with their home made choco syrup topped with your choice of ice cream. The bar has chocolate fountains with plain chocolate and milk chocolate syrup. You can dip mallows, bite size breads and fruits. Aside from the ones I mentioned, this area also served cakes and cupped desserts. Right next to it is the indian and middle eastern section, where they have a selection of biryani, dhal and couscous. Overall, the food was fantastic. The food selection was not the typical ones that we had in other hotels. Ambience of the dining area is very opulent and spotless. The staff were so-so. Most of them looked at the opposite side when you look at them. Except for the Indian lady in the dessert section, who always greets you with and smile, and ask if you need anything. And also, the Indian guest officer who handled our needs after the Filipino went away, maybe his shift was over. The Filipino told us to ask for the local water because its cheaper. 😂coz the other brand is more expensive. (10 dhs difference) We heard some friends who had distinct experience from staff. We just shrugged it off ‘til last night. *give a tip if you find the service satisfactory **we use entertainer to avail the dinner. (Do not use it, or you may be offered a cheaper water) ***a thumbs up if you find this helpful 😁 Parking: You may avail the complimentary valet parking. Wheelchair accessibility: the restaurant is accessible through elevators.

Numerous sittings with ample space in between the tables. So no need to worry to hit someone just incase the sitting got full. You may opt to be sat at their al fresco dining with the view of the marina and colorful (night time) Maqta bridge. The buffet was split into different sections. The bread and pizza section is sitting at the left side of the entrance. This area offers a variety of baked goods and hand tossed pizza with live cooking. You can basically see the chef tossing the dough, send it inside the oven and serve a steaming medium sized pizza. Pepperoni, vegetable and margherita was served that night. Next to it is the grilling section. They had a variety of tikka and kebab served, and you may choose  cuts of tuna, salmon and sea bass to be grilled. Doze it salt and pepper as you like. Right after the grilling section is the main dish area, where international cuisines were served. The selection was great, but the roasted beef ribeye is a lil bit chewy for a ribeye. The steamed veggies were nicely cooked. Not too crunchy and not too poachy. The salmon and chicken eere superb. At the end is the noodles, soup and seafood section. They served three types of soup, seafood tom yum was my wife’s must have. We’re not able to taste any of the noodles, since we had one a day ago. They have a few selections for seafood dishes, the sea-bass is not overdone. They also offer a live cooking for the seafood section, though they only had a few types of fishes offered that night. At the opposite side was the salad and sushi bar. You can watch the sushi chef prepared and hand rolled sushis. Right at the middle is the dessert bar. The area offers fresh cut and whole fruits, dates, a handful selections of arabic sweets, wide selection of ice cream, sorbet and frozen yogurt. You may also request a freshly made crepe with their home made choco syrup topped with your choice of ice cream. The bar has chocolate fountains with plain chocolate and milk chocolate syrup. You can dip mallows, bite size breads and fruits. Aside from the ones I mentioned, this area also served cakes and cupped desserts. Right next to it is the indian and middle eastern section, where they have a selection of biryani, dhal and couscous. Overall, the food was fantastic. The food selection was not the typical ones that we had in other hotels. Ambience of the dining area is very opulent and spotless. The staff were so-so. Most of them looked at the opposite side when you look at them. Except for the Indian lady in the dessert section, who always greets you with and smile, and ask if you need anything. And also, the Indian guest officer who handled our needs after the Filipino went away, maybe his shift was over. The Filipino told us to ask for the local water because its cheaper. 😂coz the other brand is more expensive. (10 dhs difference) We heard some friends who had distinct experience from staff. We just shrugged it off ‘til last night. *give a tip if you find the service satisfactory **we use entertainer to avail the dinner. (Do not use it, or you may be offered a cheaper water) ***a thumbs up if you find this helpful 😁 Parking: You may avail the complimentary valet parking. A beautiful restaurant, tastefully decorated restaurant with opulent colors to portray a regal colonial era, having indoors and waterside seating. The terrace seating overlooking the Zayed Mosque is truly breathtaking in evenings. Menu is mostly modern Northern Indian. They have a full bar along with some signature cocktails that goes in tune with a contemporary India. Service is impeccable with multiple queries regarding our comfort and food choices. The Maharaja Kebab platter was apt for sharing. Succulent flavorful meat, and no overboarding of spices. Subtle and aromatic having tandoori chicken, murgh malai, lamb chops, seekh kebab, malai jhinga and fish tikka. Jingha Biriyani though of great portion size for 2 people, lacked a depth of flavor which defines Biriyani. However, there were ample portions of prawns. A signature cocktail Rishi and a classic Negroni rounded off a great lunch. Gulab Jamun with crispy Sevyan and Rabdi exuded a warmth just like their namesake restaurant.
